conviction_note: Sum of three sized findings (+2.5, +1.5, -1.5): a $117.3M/82-aircraft P550 order whose DoD-stated completion date falls inside the reported quarter against a consensus that has Q1 product sales DOWN 2.3% y/y, plus evidence the -27% tape is sector beta and lock-up supply rather than company news, partly offset by the fact that the E-HEL award lands entirely in Q2 and has already been round-tripped by the tape; a quarter of the 11.9% implied move is as far as I will go on evidence this indirect.

findings.finding: The Army's $117,306,232 firm-fixed-price order for 82 P550 UAS carries a DoD-stated estimated completion date of 2026-07-23 -- nine days inside AeroVironment's fiscal Q1 FY27, which ended 2026-08-01 -- yet consensus has Q1 product-sales revenue at $306.4M, DOWN 2.3% year over year, a number that cannot easily absorb a ~$117M program that did not exist in the year-ago quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: The delivery schedule exists only in the DoD daily contract announcement text. AeroVironment's own press release of 2026-07-20, which is the version the sell-side reads, gives no period of performance at all and calls the order 'the initial full-rate procurement of the P550 system' -- language that invites modelling deliveries spread across FY27. If the street had the completion date, Q1 product-sales consensus would not be down 2.3% y/y and the published Q1 EPS estimates would not be scattered between $0.22 and $0.32 across aggregators. The Zacks-metric note of 2026-09-03 shows the street modelling AxS product revenue shrinking in a quarter that plausibly contains the largest single P550 delivery ever made.
findings.independence: The Defense Post reported the same contract independently on 2026-03-23 with award date 2026-03-23 and completion 'July 2026' (https://thedefensepost.com/2026/03/23/us-army-av-p550-drones/), and the segment-level consensus that it contradicts is a separate document (https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/unlocking-q1-potential-aerovironment-avav-131503275.html, 2026-09-03). Caveat I am carrying openly: award 2026-03-23 to completion 2026-07-23 straddles Q4 FY26 (ended 2026-04-30), so under percentage-of-completion some of this may already have been recognised in the $641.6M Q4 -- that is why the low end of my band is negative.

findings.finding: The -26.7% twenty-day drawdown is a documented sector-wide positioning unwind with explicitly no company news, layered on a mechanical share overhang: on 2026-08-24 AVAV fell 5% while RCAT -7%, ONDS -5%, UMAC -9% and KTOS -6%, with the report stating 'No company announcement, contract award, earnings release, regulatory action, or analyst rating change has been reported'; separately, 17,425,849 AVAV shares were issued to the BlueHalo seller and Arlington Capital sponsors, of which 40% (about 6.97M shares, roughly 5.6 days of the 1.25M-share ADV) came off lock-up on 2026-05-01 with a further 30% due 2026-11-01.
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline hands the reader '-26.73% over 20 sessions' as if it were a forecast. It is not information about this quarter. If it were, sell-side revenue estimates would have been cut -- Investing.com on the morning of the print (2026-09-09) says revenue projections 'have remained relatively stable' while only EPS moved, and five drone names with completely different balance sheets would not have fallen in lockstep on the same three sessions. The lock-up schedule is in a May-2025 8-K and appears in no preview, no wire copy and no analyst note; if it were priced, the option market would not simultaneously be paying 15.5 vol points more for calls than for puts on a stock the tape has cut in half.
findings.independence: The lock-up half of this comes from a primary SEC document filed 2026-05-01 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1368622/000110465925043118/tm2513632d1_8k.htm), which is a completely different source from the sector-beta reporting; the two point the same way for different reasons. Note this finding shares the 'read the tape' theme with finding 3, which points the other way -- they are not two votes for one conclusion.

findings.finding: The largest good news in this company's history is already spent and none of it is in tonight's numbers: the $464.8M E-HEL award (2026-09-02) is an Other Transaction Agreement ceiling for deliveries 'well into the dozens' spread over 'the next few years' -- a January Army draft solicitation sought up to 24 systems over five years -- it was awarded 32 days after the reported quarter ended, and AVAV gave back the entire intraday +6% pop it produced within four sessions and then failed to respond at all to the first international LOCUST order (>$50M, 2026-09-08).
findings.why_not_priced: Headline aggregators carried '$500 million Army contract' and 'first-ever production contract for high energy laser weapon systems in United States history'; what they did not carry is that it is an OTA ceiling over multiple years, that the funded portion is a fraction of the ceiling, and above all that it falls in fiscal Q2 and so contributes exactly zero to the funded backlog figure printed tonight -- the single line item that has repeatedly surprised on this name. Anyone in the call-heavy option positioning marking backlog up by ~$465M this evening gets nothing. If this were understood, the stock would not have round-tripped the announcement in four sessions.
findings.independence: The retracement is visible in the sealed baseline itself (5d run-up -0.38% against a reported intraday print of $153.93 on 2026-09-03, https://247wallst.com/investing/2026/09/03/aerovironment-rises-4-on-464-8m-army-laser-award-unusual-machines-and-red-cat-tick-up/). The OTA structure and the E-HEL announcement are one document cluster with AeroVironment's own release (https://www.avinc.com/2026/09/02/avs-locust-selected-for-nearly-500-million-army-counter-uas-contract-for-enduring-high-energy-laser-e-hel-program/) -- count them once.

searched_and_found_nothing: defense.gov daily contract announcements directly -- the site returns 403 to fetches, so every DoD award figure here is quoted through secondary reporting that reproduces the announcement text, and I could not build a clean funded-backlog delta for May-August 2026
California WARN notices for Simi Valley or Moorpark -- no AeroVironment filing found despite the $100M campus consolidation announced 2026-08-24

SC 13D/G or 13D/A amendments by Arlington Capital Partners showing actual disposals of the unlocked BlueHalo shares -- EDGAR full-text search returned zero hits for 2025-05-01 through 2026-09-09, so the overhang is a schedule, not a proven sale

Insider transactions -- the only Form 4 in the sell-off window is retiring director Stephen Page disposing 250 shares at $191.98 on 2026-08-17 under a 10b5-1 plan adopted 2025-09-30; no cluster, no signal

A change in reportable segments for FY27 in the FY26 10-K (filed 2026-06-29) -- could not confirm any planned realignment, so the model-breaking segment change the sweep flagged does not appear to be there

FY2027 appropriations -- a continuing resolution through 2026-12-11 was signed around 2026-09-01 (https://breakingdefense.com/2026/09/house-passes-funding-stopgap-averting-government-shutdown-in-october/), which removes the October shutdown tail but blocks new starts and production-rate increases; sector-wide, symmetric, and already known to every defense investor, so I gave it no weight

Ukraine USAI / PDA / PURL package contents naming Switchblade with a date inside the reported quarter -- nothing specific found; the Greece FMS clearance (350 Switchblade 300 Block 20, $80.1M, 2026-07-20) is an approval, not a booking
Consumer-facing angles (app store reviews, support forums, subreddits, changelogs) -- not applicable to a defense prime with no commercial product surface
The $288M Switchblade delivery order that search results served with fresh datelines -- URL path is /20250203/, February 2025, not this cycle; discarded

A material-weakness update -- the goodwill-impairment control weakness and the $89.4M Q3 FY26 restatement are from March-June 2026, fully in the wire, and the class action lead-plaintiff deadline passed 2026-07-27
baseline_tension: Findings 1 and 2 agree with the -15.5 skew (calls bid) and cut against the -26.7% run-up, which is the uncomfortable half since agreeing with the skew usually means agreeing with the price -- but finding 1 is a quarter-specific delivery date rather than sentiment, and finding 3 is a genuine offset that agrees with the tape and disagrees with the skew, so the net +2.5 is a modest tilt inside a 11.9% implied move rather than a bet on the beaten-down-name-bounces trade.
